column9: A message left for someone who is not there: 請留言, 語音留言 for voicemail, 留言板 for a message board. Online it is also a comment under a post.

column3: A teacher's way of teaching: 教法不同. The fuller word is 教学法. 法 as a way of doing something also gives 做法, 看法 and 办法.
column4: 这位老师的教法很特别。
column5: 這位老師的教法很特別。
column6: Zhè wèi lǎoshī de jiàofǎ hěn tèbié.
column7: This teacher's way of teaching is very special.
column9: A teacher's way of teaching: 教法不同. The fuller word is 教學法. 法 as a way of doing something also gives 做法, 看法 and 辦法.

column3: Mostly bound: 宗教 for religion, 信教 for following one, and 教室, 教育, 教授, 教练 where teaching is meant.
column6: Nǐ xìn jiào ma?
column7: Do you follow a religion?
column9: Mostly bound: 宗教 for religion, 信教 for following one, and 教室, 教育, 教授, 教練 where teaching is meant.

column3: Formal and respectful, mostly of an elder or a teacher: 老师的教导, 父母的教导, 教导孩子. It is about character and values more than facts.
column4: 我永远记得老师的教导。
column5: 我永遠記得老師的教導。
column6: Wǒ yǒngyuǎn jìde lǎoshī de jiàodǎo.
column7: I will always remember my teacher's guidance.
column9: Formal and respectful, mostly of an elder or a teacher: 老師的教導, 父母的教導, 教導孩子. It is about character and values more than facts.

column3: A character a student has not learned yet, from a textbook lesson: 学习生字, 生字簿. 生 means unfamiliar here, as in 生词 and 陌生; the opposite is 熟, as in 熟人.
column4: 今天老师教了十个生字。
column5: 今天老師教了十個生字。
column6: Jīntiān lǎoshī jiāo le shí ge shēngzì.
column7: The teacher taught ten new characters today.
column9: A character a student has not learned yet, from a textbook lesson: 學習生字, 生字簿. 生 means unfamiliar here, as in 生詞 and 陌生; the opposite is 熟, as in 熟人.

column3: The 会 on the end is the result: you can do it now (学会游泳, 学不会 for cannot get it). 学 alone says nothing about success. It can also mean a learned society: 学会会员.
column6: Wǒ zhōngyú xuéhuì yóuyǒng le.
column7: I finally learned to swim.
column9: The 會 on the end is the result: you can do it now (學會游泳, 學不會 for cannot get it). 學 alone says nothing about success. It can also mean a learned society: 學會會員.

column3: In Taiwan, the official name for Mandarin, as in 国语课; in everyday talk it sounds formal or old, and people mostly say 中文. The mainland says 普通话. It is not 台语, Taiwanese Hokkien.
column6: Tā de Guóyǔ shuō de hěn biāozhǔn.
column7: His Mandarin is very standard.
column9: In Taiwan, the official name for Mandarin, as in 國語課; in everyday talk it sounds formal or old, and people mostly say 中文. The mainland says 普通話. It is not 台語, Taiwanese Hokkien.

column3: A grammar term, nouns and verbs being 名词和动词, and also a plain term: 新名词, 专有名词 for a proper noun. 词 ends other parts of speech too: 动词, 形容词.
column6: Zhège míngcí hěn nán fānyì.
column7: This term is hard to translate.
column9: A grammar term, nouns and verbs being 名詞和動詞, and also a plain term: 新名詞, 專有名詞 for a proper noun. 詞 ends other parts of speech too: 動詞, 形容詞.

column3: Mostly in compounds: 中文, 英文, 作文, 文化, 文章. Language names ending in 文 point to the written or general language, and 语 to the spoken one. On its own it can mean refined: 说话很文. Its sense moved from pattern or tattoo to written glyph, then literature, then refined and cultured.
column6: Tā shuōhuà hěn wén.
column7: He speaks in a refined, bookish way.
column9: Mostly in compounds: 中文, 英文, 作文, 文化, 文章. Language names ending in 文 point to the written or general language, and 語 to the spoken one. On its own it can mean refined: 說話很文. Its sense moved from pattern or tattoo to written glyph, then literature, then refined and cultured.

column3: Mostly a bound character: the everyday verb is 翻译, and 译 turns up in 译成 (translate into), 译者, and the direction pattern 中译英 and 英译中.
column4: 这本书已经被译成英文。
column5: 這本書已經被譯成英文。
column6: Zhè běn shū yǐjīng bèi yì chéng Yīngwén.
column7: This book has already been translated into English.
column9: Mostly a bound character: the everyday verb is 翻譯, and 譯 turns up in 譯成 (translate into), 譯者, and the direction pattern 中譯英 and 英譯中.

column3: 家庭主妇 is the full, common form, and 全职主妇 stresses that running the home is her only job. The male counterpart is 主夫.
column4: 她结婚后就当了全职主妇。
column5: 她結婚後就當了全職主婦。
column6: Tā jiéhūn hòu jiù dāng le quánzhí zhǔfù.
column7: After she got married she became a full-time homemaker.
column9: 家庭主婦 is the full, common form, and 全職主婦 stresses that running the home is her only job. The male counterpart is 主夫.

column3: One of the three services, usually listed as 陆军, 海军, 空军 (army, navy, air force).
column4: 他爸爸在空军当过飞行员。
column5: 他爸爸在空軍當過飛行員。
column6: Tā bàba zài kōngjūn dāng guo fēixíngyuán.
column7: His father was a pilot in the air force.
column9: One of the three services, usually listed as 陸軍, 海軍, 空軍 (army, navy, air force).

column3: A salaried employee of a company, bank or office: 公司职员, 银行职员. For office workers as a group, speech prefers 上班族; 员工 covers everyone a company employs.
column6: Tā shì yínháng de zhíyuán.
column7: He is a bank employee.
column9: A salaried employee of a company, bank or office: 公司職員, 銀行職員. For office workers as a group, speech prefers 上班族; 員工 covers everyone a company employs.

column3: Rarely a verb on its own; it works inside compounds: 帮助, 协助, 助手, 助理, 助教. For the plain verb 'help', say 帮.
column6: Tā shì wǒ de zhù shǒu.
column7: He is my assistant.
column9: Rarely a verb on its own; it works inside compounds: 幫助, 協助, 助手, 助理, 助教. For the plain verb 'help', say 幫.

column3: Says how someone goes about tasks, so it takes a manner and describes a person: 做事认真, 做事细心, 做事马虎. 在公司做事 is also a plain way to say you work somewhere.
column6: Tā zuòshì hěn rènzhēn.
column7: He works very seriously.
column9: Says how someone goes about tasks, so it takes a manner and describes a person: 做事認真, 做事細心, 做事馬虎. 在公司做事 is also a plain way to say you work somewhere.

column3: Goes with 削铅笔 (sharpen) and 铅笔盒 (pencil case). 笔 ends the names of most writing tools: 毛笔, 钢笔. A ballpoint pen is 原子笔 in Taiwan and 圆珠笔 on the mainland.
column6: Qǐng yòng qiānbǐ xiě.
column7: Please write in pencil.
column9: Goes with 削鉛筆 (sharpen) and 鉛筆盒 (pencil case). 筆 ends the names of most writing tools: 毛筆, 鋼筆. A ballpoint pen is 原子筆 in Taiwan and 圓珠筆 on the mainland.

column3: Written style, with two jobs: 所谓A，就是B defines a term, and 所谓的专家 puts a doubting tone on 'so-called experts'. The word that follows is the thing being named or questioned.
column4: 所谓幸福，就是和家人在一起。
column5: 所謂幸福，就是和家人在一起。
column6: Suǒwèi xìngfú, jiùshì hé jiārén zài yīqǐ.
column7: What is called happiness is being together with family.
column9: Written style, with two jobs: 所謂A，就是B defines a term, and 所謂的專家 puts a doubting tone on 'so-called experts'. The word that follows is the thing being named or questioned.

column3: Switches to a separate or less central topic, often after saying what you do know: 至于他，我不知道. 不至于 means 'it won't go that far', as in 不至于这么严重吧.
column4: 我只知道这些，至于其他的我不清楚。
column5: 我只知道這些，至於其他的我不清楚。
column6: Wǒ zhǐ zhīdào zhèxiē, zhìyú qítā de wǒ bù qīngchu.
column7: I only know this much; as for the rest, I'm not sure.
column9: Switches to a separate or less central topic, often after saying what you do know: 至於他，我不知道. 不至於 means 'it won't go that far', as in 不至於這麼嚴重吧.

column3: Official, written style for plans and recorded details: 变更日期, 变更地址, 变更计划. For something changing in a person, use 改变.
column6: Huìyì shíjiān yǐjīng biàngēng le.
column7: The meeting time has been changed.
column9: Official, written style for plans and recorded details: 變更日期, 變更地址, 變更計劃. For something changing in a person, use 改變.

column3: The opposite of 进步, usually about skill or results: 成绩退步, 退步了. For giving ground in a negotiation the usual word is 让步.
column6: Tā zhè cì de chéngjì tuìbù le.
column7: His grades have dropped this time.
column9: The opposite of 進步, usually about skill or results: 成績退步, 退步了. For giving ground in a negotiation the usual word is 讓步.

column3: The new thing is the subject and the old is the object: 机器取代人, or passive 被取代. It means pushing the old out; 代替 is the milder word for standing in for someone, as in 代替我去.
column6: Shǒujī qǔdài le hěn duō dōngxi.
column7: Smartphones have replaced many things.
column9: The new thing is the subject and the old is the object: 機器取代人, or passive 被取代. It means pushing the old out; 代替 is the milder word for standing in for someone, as in 代替我去.

column6: Wǒ huì jìn lì bāng nǐ.
column7: I will do my best to help you.

column3: Two uses: 好久不见 is the greeting, and with 了 it says something is gone: 钱包不见了. It does not mean 'cannot see'; for that say 看不见.
column6: Hǎojiǔ bùjiàn!
column7: Long time no see!
column9: Two uses: 好久不見 is the greeting, and with 了 it says something is gone: 錢包不見了. It does not mean 'cannot see'; for that say 看不見.

column3: Name the missing thing first: 钱包不见了. It only says it is no longer there, often without knowing why; 丢了 says it is lost. For a missing person, news and police say 失踪.
column6: Wǒ de shǒujī bùjiànle.
column7: My phone is missing.
column9: Name the missing thing first: 錢包不見了. It only says it is no longer there, often without knowing why; 丟了 says it is lost. For a missing person, news and police say 失蹤.

column3: Almost always inside compounds: 工作, 作业, 作文, 作用, 作家, 作为. 做 covers concrete everyday doing (做饭, 做事), while 作 leans to abstract or formal words. 做 began as a variant of 作.
column6: Wǒ xiě wán zuò yè jiù shuìjiào.
column7: I go to sleep once I finish my homework.
column9: Almost always inside compounds: 工作, 作業, 作文, 作用, 作家, 作為. 做 covers concrete everyday doing (做飯, 做事), while 作 leans to abstract or formal words. 做 began as a variant of 作.

column3: Talks about character and manners: 做人要诚实, 会做人 ('knows how to get along'). It does not mean 'become a person'. It pairs with 做事, how one handles tasks.
column6: Zuòrén yào chéngshí.
column7: One must be honest in life.
column9: Talks about character and manners: 做人要誠實, 會做人 ('knows how to get along'). It does not mean 'become a person'. It pairs with 做事, how one handles tasks.

column3: Mostly in compounds: 照顾 (take care of), 顾客 (customer), 顾虑 (worry). Alone, 顾 as in 顾店 or 顾小孩 is an everyday verb in Taiwan; the mainland more often says 看店, 看孩子.
column6: Zhè jiā diàn de gù kè hěn duō.
column7: This shop has a lot of customers.
column9: Mostly in compounds: 照顧 (take care of), 顧客 (customer), 顧慮 (worry). Alone, 顧 as in 顧店 or 顧小孩 is an everyday verb in Taiwan; the mainland more often says 看店, 看孩子.

column3: Both verb and noun: 对社会有贡献, 做出贡献. A respectful, written word for giving effort, time or talent to a group or cause, not for handing over a thing.
column4: 他对社会有很大的贡献。
column5: 他對社會有很大的貢獻。
column6: Tā duì shèhuì yǒu hěn dà de gòngxiàn.
column7: He has made a great contribution to society.
column9: Both verb and noun: 對社會有貢獻, 做出貢獻. A respectful, written word for giving effort, time or talent to a group or cause, not for handing over a thing.

column3: Formal: helping with a task that someone else leads, usually in an organization: 协助警方, 协助调查. Ordinary help between people is 帮助 or 帮忙.
column4: 请协助我们完成这件事。
column5: 請協助我們完成這件事。
column6: Qǐng xiézhù wǒmen wánchéng zhè jiàn shì.
column7: Please help us finish this matter.
column9: Formal: helping with a task that someone else leads, usually in an organization: 協助警方, 協助調查. Ordinary help between people is 幫助 or 幫忙.

column3: The thing used goes before it: 这个词的用法. Also printed on medicine and product labels, often as 用法用量 (directions and dose).
column4: 这个词的用法我还不太懂。
column5: 這個詞的用法我還不太懂。
column6: Zhège cí de yòngfǎ wǒ hái bù tài dǒng.
column7: I don't quite understand how to use this word yet.
column9: The thing used goes before it: 這個詞的用法. Also printed on medicine and product labels, often as 用法用量 (directions and dose).

column3: The everyday word for the often unwritten rules of a home, school or group: 守规矩, 立规矩, 没规矩. As an adjective it praises behavior: 这孩子很规矩. 规则 and 规定 are the written kinds.
column6: Zài zhèlǐ yào shǒu guīju.
column7: You must follow the rules here.
column9: The everyday word for the often unwritten rules of a home, school or group: 守規矩, 立規矩, 沒規矩. As an adjective it praises behavior: 這孩子很規矩. 規則 and 規定 are the written kinds.

column3: Used with a number to cap it: 限五人, 限时. It also forms 限制, 有限 and 期限, and 名额有限 means places are limited.
column6: Měi rén xiàn mǎi liǎng ge.
column7: Limit two per person.
column9: Used with a number to cap it: 限五人, 限時. It also forms 限制, 有限 and 期限, and 名額有限 means places are limited.

column3: Written style; it opens a sentence to give the source: 据说, 据报道, 据我所知. In compounds it also means 'basis': 根据, 数据.
column4: 据新闻报导，明天会下雨。
column5: 據新聞報導，明天會下雨。
column6: Jù xīnwén bàodǎo, míngtiān huì xiàyǔ.
column7: According to the news, it will rain tomorrow.
column9: Written style; it opens a sentence to give the source: 據說, 據報道, 據我所知. In compounds it also means 'basis': 根據, 數據.

column3: Written style: it opens the second clause and names a bad result you want to avoid, after the clause that says what to do. It cannot be used with a good outcome. In speech 免得 is similar.
column6: Zǎodiǎn chūmén, yǐmiǎn chídào.
column7: Leave early so you won't be late.
column9: Written style: it opens the second clause and names a bad result you want to avoid, after the clause that says what to do. It cannot be used with a good outcome. In speech 免得 is similar.

column3: Spoken, and mostly in negatives: 不要紧 is the usual reply to an apology, and 没什么要紧 reassures that something is not serious. 重要 is the plainer word for importance.
column4: 这件事很要紧，不能忘记。
column5: 這件事很要緊，不能忘記。
column6: Zhè jiàn shì hěn yàojǐn, bù néng wàngjì.
column7: This matter is important, and must not be forgotten.
column9: Spoken, and mostly in negatives: 不要緊 is the usual reply to an apology, and 沒什麼要緊 reassures that something is not serious. 重要 is the plainer word for importance.

column3: Formal as a stand-alone word; speech says 比如 or 像. It builds many words: 如果, 例如, 如何, 不如 ('not as good as; had better', as in 你不如问问他).
column4: 本店出售各种水果，如苹果、香蕉等。
column5: 本店出售各種水果，如蘋果、香蕉等。
column6: Běn diàn chūshòu gèzhǒng shuǐguǒ, rú píngguǒ, xiāngjiāo děng.
column7: This shop sells all kinds of fruit, such as apples and bananas.
column9: Formal as a stand-alone word; speech says 比如 or 像. It builds many words: 如果, 例如, 如何, 不如 ('not as good as; had better', as in 你不如問問他).

column3: Spoken; the second clause usually has 也 or 还是: 就算下雨，我也要去. 即使 is the written equivalent. At the end of a sentence 就算了 means 'forget it': 不想去就算了.
column6: Jiùsuàn xiàyǔ, wǒ yě yào qù.
column7: Even if it rains, I will go.
column9: Spoken; the second clause usually has 也 or 還是: 就算下雨，我也要去. 即使 is the written equivalent. At the end of a sentence 就算了 means 'forget it': 不想去就算了.

column3: Shows a firm decision or demand, usually at the start, followed by 都 or 也: 无论如何你都要来. Speech often says 不管怎么样 instead.
column6: Wúlùnrúhé, wǒ dōu huì qù.
column7: No matter what, I will go.
column9: Shows a firm decision or demand, usually at the start, followed by 都 or 也: 無論如何你都要來. Speech often says 不管怎麼樣 instead.

column3: Sets up a window of time that will close, then says what to do in it: 趁热, 趁年轻, 趁早, 趁机会. The time word comes right after 趁, and 趁着 is a common longer form.
column6: Chèn rè chī ba.
column7: Eat it while it's hot.
column9: Sets up a window of time that will close, then says what to do in it: 趁熱, 趁年輕, 趁早, 趁機會. The time word comes right after 趁, and 趁著 is a common longer form.

column3: Mostly asked as a question or said in the negative: 受不了 is the common way to say 'I can't stand it', and it is used for annoyance too. The pattern V得了 / V不了 also gives 吃不了 and 忘不了. 了 is read liǎo here: it is used with 得 or 不 after a verb.
column4: 这么热的天气，你受得了吗？
column5: 這麼熱的天氣，你受得了嗎？
column6: Zhème rè de tiānqì, nǐ shòudeliǎo ma?
column7: Can you stand such hot weather?
column9: Mostly asked as a question or said in the negative: 受不了 is the common way to say 'I can't stand it', and it is used for annoyance too. The pattern V得了 / V不了 also gives 吃不了 and 忘不了. 了 is read liǎo here: it is used with 得 or 不 after a verb.

column3: Goes before a verb and is about agreeing to do it, so it shows up mostly in refusals: 不肯, 肯不肯? 愿意 is the warmer word for being glad to. Also in 肯定.
column6: Tā bù kěn gàosu wǒ.
column7: He refuses to tell me.
column9: Goes before a verb and is about agreeing to do it, so it shows up mostly in refusals: 不肯, 肯不肯? 愿意 is the warmer word for being glad to. Also in 肯定.

column3: Formal; seen in awards, ads and advice: 最佳男主角, 最佳选择, 最佳时机. In speech people say 最好.
column6: Zhè shì zuìjiā de xuǎnzé.
column7: This is the best choice.
column9: Formal; seen in awards, ads and advice: 最佳男主角, 最佳選擇, 最佳時機. In speech people say 最好.

column3: Goes with 语言障碍, 沟通障碍 and 克服障碍. 无障碍 means 'accessible', as on signs and in 无障碍厕所 and 无障碍设施.
column6: Yǔyán bù shì wǒmen de zhàng'ài.
column7: Language is not our obstacle.
column9: Goes with 語言障礙, 溝通障礙 and 克服障礙. 無障礙 means 'accessible', as on signs and in 無障礙廁所 and 無障礙設施.

column3: Describes a situation, scene or system: 交通混乱, 局势混乱. It sounds more serious and formal than the everyday 乱, which can describe a messy room.
column6: Xiàbān shíjiān lùshang hěn hùnluàn.
column7: The roads are chaotic at rush hour.
column9: Describes a situation, scene or system: 交通混亂, 局勢混亂. It sounds more serious and formal than the everyday 亂, which can describe a messy room.

column3: Praises a life, a schedule or content that is busy in a good way: 生活很充实. As a verb it means 'to enrich': 充实自己 is to build up your knowledge or skills.
column6: Wǒ de dàxué shēnghuó hěn chōngshí.
column7: My college life is very full.
column9: Praises a life, a schedule or content that is busy in a good way: 生活很充實. As a verb it means 'to enrich': 充實自己 is to build up your knowledge or skills.

column3: Used for the standard of quality or skill: 水准很高, 生活水准, 提高水准. The mainland leans to 水平 for the same idea, while 水准 is common in Taiwan.
column6: Zhè jiā cāntīng de shuǐzhǔn hěn gāo.
column7: This restaurant's standard is very high.
column9: Used for the standard of quality or skill: 水准很高, 生活水准, 提高水准. The mainland leans to 水平 for the same idea, while 水准 is common in Taiwan.

column3: Written or serious style: 文化差异, 个别差异, 差异很大. Speech uses 不一样, 区别 or 差别.
column4: 两个地方的文化差异很大。
column5: 兩個地方的文化差異很大。
column6: Liǎng ge dìfang de wénhuà chāyì hěn dà.
column7: The cultures of the two places are very different.
column9: Written or serious style: 文化差異, 個別差異, 差異很大. Speech uses 不一樣, 區別 or 差別.

column3: Describes a feeling that is not put on. It works as a noun after 的 (一片真心), or as an adverb before a verb: 真心喜欢, 真心想帮你. 真心话 means words from the heart.
column6: Wǒ shì zhēnxīn xiǎng bāng nǐ.
column7: I sincerely want to help you.
column9: Describes a feeling that is not put on. It works as a noun after 的 (一片真心), or as an adverb before a verb: 真心喜歡, 真心想幫你. 真心話 means words from the heart.

column3: Two uses: an intensifier before a noun or adjective (真是个好人), and in speech a grumble at someone, present or not: 你真是的！, 真是的，又迟到了.
column4: 你真是的，又忘了带钥匙！
column5: 你真是的，又忘了帶鑰匙！
column6: Nǐ zhēnshi de, yòu wàng le dài yàoshi!
column7: Honestly, you forgot your keys again!
column9: Two uses: an intensifier before a noun or adjective (真是個好人), and in speech a grumble at someone, present or not: 你真是的！, 真是的，又遲到了.

column3: The act pretended follows it: 假装不知道, 假装睡觉, 假装生气. 装 alone also fakes things: 装病, 装傻.
column6: Tā jiǎzhuāng méi kànjiàn wǒ.
column7: He pretended not to see me.
column9: The act pretended follows it: 假裝不知道, 假裝睡覺, 假裝生氣. 裝 alone also fakes things: 裝病, 裝傻.

column3: Of water, air, sound or an image: 水很清, 看清, 清楚, 清洁. As a verb it means to clear up or settle: 清账, 清理. It is also the name of the Qing dynasty, 清朝.
column6: Zhèlǐ de shuǐ hěn qīng.
column7: The water here is very clear.
column9: Of water, air, sound or an image: 水很清, 看清, 清楚, 清潔. As a verb it means to clear up or settle: 清帳, 清理. It is also the name of the Qing dynasty, 清朝.

column3: Comes before the clause that turned out well, often against a bad possibility that was avoided: 幸好没下雨. It can mostly be swapped with 幸亏, which points more to a cause.
column6: Xìnghǎo wǒ dài le yǔsǎn.
column7: Fortunately I brought an umbrella.
column9: Comes before the clause that turned out well, often against a bad possibility that was avoided: 幸好沒下雨. It can mostly be swapped with 幸虧, which points more to a cause.

column3: Close to 幸好 and just as common in speech; it often names what saved the situation, usually a person or an action: 幸亏有你.
column6: Xìngkuī nǐ tíxǐng wǒ.
column7: Luckily you reminded me.
column9: Close to 幸好 and just as common in speech; it often names what saved the situation, usually a person or an action: 幸虧有你.

column3: Found in compounds: 似乎 (formal, with a note of doubt), 相似, 类似, 好似. After a noun, 似的 means 'as if': 像雪似的.
column6: Tā sì hū hěn lèi.
column7: He seems very tired.
column9: Found in compounds: 似乎 (formal, with a note of doubt), 相似, 類似, 好似. After a noun, 似的 means 'as if': 像雪似的.

column3: Stresses that someone did it without help, often with feeling behind it: a gift made, a meal cooked, a letter handed over. 亲 + body part forms a set: 亲手, 亲眼, 亲耳, 亲口. 亲自 means 'in person' instead.
column4: 这是妈妈亲手做的蛋糕。
column5: 這是媽媽親手做的蛋糕。
column6: Zhè shì māma qīnshǒu zuò de dàngāo.
column7: This is a cake Mom made with her own hands.
column9: Stresses that someone did it without help, often with feeling behind it: a gift made, a meal cooked, a letter handed over. 親 + body part forms a set: 親手, 親眼, 親耳, 親口. 親自 means 'in person' instead.

column3: Stresses that you saw it yourself, so it is true: 亲眼看到, 亲眼所见. Same set as 亲手; for hearing it yourself the word is 亲耳.
column6: Wǒ qīnyǎn kànjiàn tā jìnqù le.
column7: I saw him go in with my own eyes.
column9: Stresses that you saw it yourself, so it is true: 親眼看到, 親眼所見. Same set as 親手; for hearing it yourself the word is 親耳.

column3: It goes before the verb and means face to face, not through a message or behind someone's back: 当面说, 当面道谢, 当面问清楚.
column6: Wǒ xiǎng dāngmiàn gēn tā dàoxiè.
column7: I want to thank him in person.
column9: It goes before the verb and means face to face, not through a message or behind someone's back: 當面說, 當面道謝, 當面問清楚.

column3: An adverb before the verb: you went out of your way, on purpose, for this one thing (特地来看你, 特地为你准备). 特意 is much the same.
column6: Tā tèdì cóng Táizhōng lái kàn wǒ.
column7: He came all the way from Taichung just to see me.
column9: An adverb before the verb: you went out of your way, on purpose, for this one thing (特地來看你, 特地為你準備). 特意 is much the same.

column3: Goes before the verb to add a small extra errand to a trip you are making anyway: 顺便买, 顺便问一下. 顺便说一句 opens an aside, "by the way".
column4: 你出去的时候，顺便帮我买杯咖啡。
column5: 你出去的時候，順便幫我買杯咖啡。
column6: Nǐ chūqù de shíhou, shùnbiàn bāng wǒ mǎi bēi kāfēi.
column7: When you go out, get me a coffee while you're at it.
column9: Goes before the verb to add a small extra errand to a trip you are making anyway: 順便買, 順便問一下. 順便說一句 opens an aside, "by the way".

column3: A written, polite word for 一起 (一同前往, 一同参加); in everyday speech say 一起. It comes before the verb, and the person is added with 与 or 和: 与大家一同.
column6: Huānyíng dàjiā yītóng cānjiā.
column7: Everyone is welcome to join in together.
column9: A written, polite word for 一起 (一同前往, 一同參加); in everyday speech say 一起. It comes before the verb, and the person is added with 與 or 和: 與大家一同.

column3: Mostly a building block: 同班, 同年, 同事, 同学, 同意, 不同. As "with" it is written style (同他商量); speech uses 跟 or 和.
column6: Wǒ hé tā tóng bān.
column7: He and I are in the same class.
column9: Mostly a building block: 同班, 同年, 同事, 同學, 同意, 不同. As "with" it is written style (同他商量); speech uses 跟 or 和.

column3: A deliberate look back at the past: 回想起来, 回想当时. 回忆 is the close neighbor and is also the noun for memories (美好的回忆), while 回想 is mainly the verb.
column4: 回想起来，那是一段快乐的时光。
column5: 回想起來，那是一段快樂的時光。
column6: Huíxiǎng qǐlái, nà shì yī duàn kuàilè de shíguāng.
column7: Thinking back, it was a happy time.
column9: A deliberate look back at the past: 回想起來, 回想當時. 回憶 is the close neighbor and is also the noun for memories (美好的回憶), while 回想 is mainly the verb.

column3: Works as a verb (想像一下, 无法想像, 难以想像) and as a noun (想像力). The mainland usually writes it 想象.
column4: 我无法想像没有手机的生活。
column5: 我無法想像沒有手機的生活。
column6: Wǒ wúfǎ xiǎngxiàng méiyǒu shǒujī de shēnghuó.
column7: I can't imagine life without a phone.
column9: Works as a verb (想像一下, 無法想像, 難以想像) and as a noun (想像力). The mainland usually writes it 想象.

column3: The pattern is 把A当作B: A is taken as B, sometimes only as a pretense (当作没看见). 当成 and 当做 mean the same. 当 is read dàng here, with the sense "to regard as".
column6: Tā bǎ wǒ dàngzuò péngyou.
column7: He treats me as a friend.
column9: The pattern is 把A當作B: A is taken as B, sometimes only as a pretense (當作沒看見). 當成 and 當做 mean the same. 當 is read dàng here, with the sense "to regard as".

column3: The same word as 当作, in the same 把A当做B pattern, also for pretending (当做没发生). 当成 is a third version. 做 was originally a vulgar variant of 作.
column4: 他把这里当做自己的家。
column5: 他把這裡當做自己的家。
column6: Tā bǎ zhèlǐ dàngzuò zìjǐ de jiā.
column7: He treats this place as his own home.
column9: The same word as 當作, in the same 把A當做B pattern, also for pretending (當做沒發生). 當成 is a third version. 做 was originally a vulgar variant of 作.

column3: Rarely a word on its own: speech uses 知道. It lives in compounds such as 通知, 知识, 知名, 无知. In oracle bone inscriptions it was an adult, a mouth and a child, "to transmit knowledge"; it was originally the same character as 智.
column6: Wǒ bù zhī dao tā zài nǎlǐ.
column7: I don't know where he is.
column9: Rarely a word on its own: speech uses 知道. It lives in compounds such as 通知, 知識, 知名, 無知. In oracle bone inscriptions it was an adult, a mouth and a child, "to transmit knowledge"; it was originally the same character as 智.

column3: What you take away from a course, a book or an experience, named after its topic: 学习心得, 读书心得. You 写心得 or 分享心得, and a 心得报告 is a typical school assignment.
column4: 他分享了学习中文的心得。
column5: 他分享了學習中文的心得。
column6: Tā fēnxiǎng le xuéxí Zhōngwén de xīndé.
column7: He shared what he has learned from studying Chinese.
column9: What you take away from a course, a book or an experience, named after its topic: 學習心得, 讀書心得. You 寫心得 or 分享心得, and a 心得報告 is a typical school assignment.

column3: The thought behind a gift or a favor. The giver says it humbly (一点心意, 一点小小的心意); the receiver thanks the thought: 谢谢你的心意.
column6: Zhè shì wǒ de yīdiǎn xīnyì.
column7: This is a small token from me.
column9: The thought behind a gift or a favor. The giver says it humbly (一點心意, 一點小小的心意); the receiver thanks the thought: 謝謝你的心意.

column3: Deep wisdom about life and people (人生的智慧, 有智慧). In technology, Taiwan uses it for "smart": 智慧型手机 and 智慧财产权, where the mainland says 智能手机 and 知识产权.
column6: Lǎorén yǒu fēngfù de zhìhuì.
column7: Old people have rich wisdom.
column9: Deep wisdom about life and people (人生的智慧, 有智慧). In technology, Taiwan uses it for "smart": 智慧型手機 and 智慧財產權, where the mainland says 智能手機 and 知識產權.

column3: The subject (哲学系, 哲学家) and also a personal outlook: 人生哲学, 生活哲学. A person you call 哲学家 may simply be a deep thinker.
column6: Tā zài dàxué dú zhéxué.
column7: He studies philosophy in college.
column9: The subject (哲學系, 哲學家) and also a personal outlook: 人生哲學, 生活哲學. A person you call 哲學家 may simply be a deep thinker.

column3: Said of a person others should copy, often a parent, teacher or older sibling: 好榜样, 做榜样, 以…为榜样 (take as a model).
column6: Gēge shì dìdi de bǎngyàng.
column7: The older brother is the younger brother's role model.
column9: Said of a person others should copy, often a parent, teacher or older sibling: 好榜樣, 做榜樣, 以…為榜樣 (take as a model).

column3: Goes with 信仰 and 自由 (宗教信仰, 宗教自由). Names of religions end in 教: 佛教, 道教, 基督教.
column4: 台湾有很多不同的宗教。
column5: 台灣有很多不同的宗教。
column6: Táiwān yǒu hěn duō bùtóng de zōngjiào.
column7: There are many different religions in Taiwan.
column9: Goes with 信仰 and 自由 (宗教信仰, 宗教自由). Names of religions end in 教: 佛教, 道教, 基督教.

column3: The religion, with temples, priests (道士) and rituals, not 道家, the philosophy of Laozi and Zhuangzi. 信道教 means to follow it.
column6: Hěn duō Táiwānrén xìnyǎng Dàojiào.
column7: Many Taiwanese follow Daoism.
column9: The religion, with temples, priests (道士) and rituals, not 道家, the philosophy of Laozi and Zhuangzi. 信道教 means to follow it.

column3: 信佛教 means to be Buddhist, and 信佛 is the shorter way to say it. A follower is a 佛教徒, and 拜佛 is to worship the Buddha.
column6: Tā xìn Fójiào.
column7: He is Buddhist.
column9: 信佛教 means to be Buddhist, and 信佛 is the shorter way to say it. A follower is a 佛教徒, and 拜佛 is to worship the Buddha.

column3: In everyday Chinese this usually means Protestantism; Catholicism is the separate 天主教. A believer is a 基督徒, and a congregation a 基督教会.
column6: Tāmen jiā xìn Jīdūjiào.
column7: Their family is Christian.
column9: In everyday Chinese this usually means Protestantism; Catholicism is the separate 天主教. A believer is a 基督徒, and a congregation a 基督教會.

column3: The usual word for God among Protestants (Catholics say 天主, and 神 is also used): 相信上帝, 感谢上帝. In oracle bone inscriptions 帝 already wrote the word for the supreme deity, who commands rain, thunder, and wind.
column6: Gǎnxiè Shàngdì, nǐ méi shì!
column7: Thank God, you're okay!
column9: The usual word for God among Protestants (Catholics say 天主, and 神 is also used): 相信上帝, 感謝上帝. In oracle bone inscriptions 帝 already wrote the word for the supreme deity, who commands rain, thunder, and wind.

column3: The religious heaven (上天堂; opposite 地狱), and any place famous for one thing: 购物天堂, 美食天堂. For the sky itself say 天空.
column6: Zhèlǐ shì měishí de tiāntáng.
column7: This place is a paradise for food.
column9: The religious heaven (上天堂; opposite 地獄), and any place famous for one thing: 購物天堂, 美食天堂. For the sky itself say 天空.

column3: A religious or literary word, set against the body (灵魂与身体, 灵魂深处). It is also the core of something: 球队的灵魂人物.
column6: Tā xiāngxìn rén yǒu línghún.
column7: He believes that people have a soul.
column9: A religious or literary word, set against the body (靈魂與身體, 靈魂深處). It is also the core of something: 球隊的靈魂人物.

column3: The everyday word for a temple, especially of Daoist or folk religion, with a deity (妈祖庙); 寺 is mainly Buddhist and in names. Counted with 座: 一座庙. 庙会 is the temple fair.
column6: Zhè zuò miào hěn yǒumíng.
column7: This temple is very famous.
column9: The everyday word for a temple, especially of Daoist or folk religion, with a deity (媽祖廟); 寺 is mainly Buddhist and in names. Counted with 座: 一座廟. 廟會 is the temple fair.

column3: Buddhist, Daoist and folk temples together, from 寺 (mainly Buddhist; it also names mosques, 清真寺) and 庙. 参观寺庙 is a typical outing.
column4: 这座寺庙已经有三百年的历史。
column5: 這座寺廟已經有三百年的歷史。
column6: Zhè zuò sìmiào yǐjīng yǒu sān bǎi nián de lìshǐ.
column7: This temple has a history of three hundred years.
column9: Buddhist, Daoist and folk temples together, from 寺 (mainly Buddhist; it also names mosques, 清真寺) and 廟. 參觀寺廟 is a typical outing.

column3: The church building; the congregation is 教会. Go there 做礼拜 or 去教堂; a Catholic church is 天主教堂. 堂 as a hall is also in 礼堂 and 课堂.
column6: Tāmen xīngqītiān qù jiàotáng.
column7: They go to church on Sundays.
column9: The church building; the congregation is 教會. Go there 做禮拜 or 去教堂; a Catholic church is 天主教堂. 堂 as a hall is also in 禮堂 and 課堂.

column3: Recommend a thing or person, often to someone: 推荐一本书给我. Also to put someone forward (老师推荐我), and 推荐信 is a reference letter. 有什么推荐的吗？ asks a waiter or a friend.
column4: 你可以推荐一本书给我吗？
column5: 你可以推薦一本書給我嗎？
column6: Nǐ kěyǐ tuījiàn yī běn shū gěi wǒ ma?
column7: Can you recommend a book to me?
column9: Recommend a thing or person, often to someone: 推薦一本書給我. Also to put someone forward (老師推薦我), and 推薦信 is a reference letter. 有什麼推薦的嗎？ asks a waiter or a friend.

column3: Mostly 说实话, "to tell the truth", which often opens a frank opinion, especially a negative one. Also 实话实说 (say it as it is) and 老实话.
column6: Shuō shíhuà, wǒ bù xǐhuan zhège.
column7: To tell the truth, I don't like this one.
column9: Mostly 說實話, "to tell the truth", which often opens a frank opinion, especially a negative one. Also 實話實說 (say it as it is) and 老實話.

column3: A written word for a field of knowledge, work or activity: 专业领域, 科学领域, 在…领域. A person is an expert 在这个领域, not in a physical field.
column6: Tā shì zhège lǐngyù de zhuānjiā.
column7: He is an expert in this field.
column9: A written word for a field of knowledge, work or activity: 專業領域, 科學領域, 在…領域. A person is an expert 在這個領域, not in a physical field.

column3: A king. Other royals follow the pattern: 女王 is a reigning queen, 王后 a king's wife, 王子 a prince, 王国 a kingdom. 王 is possibly a picture of a ritual axe, perhaps of jade, a symbol of the king's power.
column6: Guówáng zhù zài chéngbǎo lǐ.
column7: The king lives in a castle.
column9: A king. Other royals follow the pattern: 女王 is a reigning queen, 王后 a king's wife, 王子 a prince, 王國 a kingdom. 王 is possibly a picture of a ritual axe, perhaps of jade, a symbol of the king's power.

column3: Both the noun (总统选举, 参加选举, 选举结果) and the verb (选举总统). To vote is 投票, and for plain "choose" say 选. Xu Shen argues that 选 originally meant to respectfully reject and send someone back, and that choosing implies rejecting the others.
column4: 台湾的总统选举每四年一次。
column5: 台灣的總統選舉每四年一次。
column6: Táiwān de zǒngtǒng xuǎnjǔ měi sì nián yī cì.
column7: Taiwan's presidential election is held every four years.
column9: Both the noun (總統選舉, 參加選舉, 選舉結果) and the verb (選舉總統). To vote is 投票, and for plain "choose" say 選. Xu Shen argues that 選 originally meant to respectfully reject and send someone back, and that choosing implies rejecting the others.

column3: Used for historical revolutions (工业革命, 辛亥革命), a person (革命家) and any sweeping change (技术革命). It can be a verb, "to revolt".
column6: Gōngyè gémìng gǎibiàn le shìjiè.
column7: The Industrial Revolution changed the world.
column9: Used for historical revolutions (工業革命, 辛亥革命), a person (革命家) and any sweeping change (技術革命). It can be a verb, "to revolt".

column3: In Taiwan years are counted from the Republic's founding in 1912: 民国115年 is 2026 (add 1911). Forms, receipts and the news use it. On the mainland it names the 1912 to 1949 period (民国时期).
column4: 今年是民国一百一十五年。
column5: 今年是民國一百一十五年。
column6: Jīnnián shì Mínguó yībǎiyīshíwǔ nián.
column7: This year is the 115th year of the Republic.
column9: In Taiwan years are counted from the Republic's founding in 1912: 民國115年 is 2026 (add 1911). Forms, receipts and the news use it. On the mainland it names the 1912 to 1949 period (民國時期).

column3: Goes with 时期 and with the ruling country: 殖民地时期, 荷兰的殖民地. 殖民 alone is the act or the adjective (殖民主义, colonialism).
column4: 台湾曾经是荷兰的殖民地。
column5: 台灣曾經是荷蘭的殖民地。
column6: Táiwān céngjīng shì Hélán de zhímíndì.
column7: Taiwan was once a Dutch colony.
column9: Goes with 時期 and with the ruling country: 殖民地時期, 荷蘭的殖民地. 殖民 alone is the act or the adjective (殖民主義, colonialism).

column3: Mostly corruption of officials and institutions (政治腐败, 反腐败 for anti-corruption). It also means rotten, but for food speech says 坏了 or 变质. 败 possibly began with the sense "to break", which later narrowed.
column4: 政府腐败让人民很失望。
column5: 政府腐敗讓人民很失望。
column6: Zhèngfǔ fǔbài ràng rénmín hěn shīwàng.
column7: Government corruption disappoints the people greatly.
column9: Mostly corruption of officials and institutions (政治腐敗, 反腐敗 for anti-corruption). It also means rotten, but for food speech says 壞了 or 變質. 敗 possibly began with the sense "to break", which later narrowed.

column3: A verb with its object built in, so time and aspect go between: 打了三年仗, 打过仗. For a fight between people use 打架.
column6: Liǎng ge guójiā dǎzhàng le.
column7: The two countries went to war.
column9: A verb with its object built in, so time and aspect go between: 打了三年仗, 打過仗. For a fight between people use 打架.

column3: The armed forces as a whole or a unit, counted with 支: 一支军队. One soldier is a 军人 or 士兵. 队 is also in 球队 and 队长.
column6: Jūnduì jìnrù le chéngshì.
column7: The troops entered the city.
column9: The armed forces as a whole or a unit, counted with 支: 一支軍隊. One soldier is a 軍人 or 士兵. 隊 is also in 球隊 and 隊長.

column3: An armed robber or bandit, a word of stories and news that now sounds a bit old-fashioned. Taiwan usually says 抢匪 for a robber, the mainland 劫匪.
column6: Qiángdào qiǎngzǒu le tā de qián.
column7: The robbers took his money.
column9: An armed robber or bandit, a word of stories and news that now sounds a bit old-fashioned. Taiwan usually says 搶匪 for a robber, the mainland 劫匪.

column3: A thief who steals quietly: 抓小偷. A pickpocket is 扒手, and a robber who uses force 强盗. 小 is just a prefix, not "little". 偷 also means "secretly" in 偷偷 (偷偷地走).
column6: Xiǎotōu tōuzǒu le wǒ de qiánbāo.
column7: The thief stole my wallet.
column9: A thief who steals quietly: 抓小偷. A pickpocket is 扒手, and a robber who uses force 強盜. 小 is just a prefix, not "little". 偷 also means "secretly" in 偷偷 (偷偷地走).

column3: Takes something bad as its object: 犯错, 犯法, 犯罪. It also means falling into a bad state: 犯困 (get sleepy), 犯愁 (worry); 犯病 is an illness flaring up. As a noun it is a criminal: 罪犯, 犯人. The sense is traced from "to pass over" to "to offend against, oppose".
column6: Měi ge rén dōu huì fàn cuò.
column7: Everyone makes mistakes.
column9: Takes something bad as its object: 犯錯, 犯法, 犯罪. It also means falling into a bad state: 犯睏 (get sleepy), 犯愁 (worry); 犯病 is an illness flaring up. As a noun it is a criminal: 罪犯, 犯人. The sense is traced from "to pass over" to "to offend against, oppose".

column3: The stronger side mistreats the weaker, as in school: 被欺负, 欺负人. Between friends or couples 别欺负我 can be a half-joking protest.
column6: Tā chángcháng bèi tóngxué qīfu.
column7: He is often bullied by classmates.
column9: The stronger side mistreats the weaker, as in school: 被欺負, 欺負人. Between friends or couples 別欺負我 can be a half-joking protest.

column3: Giving up a life or something valued for others or a cause: 为国牺牲, 牺牲自己, 牺牲睡眠. As a noun it is the cost itself: 很大的牺牲.
column4: 他为了家人牺牲了很多。
column5: 他為了家人犧牲了很多。
column6: Tā wèile jiārén xīshēng le hěn duō.
column7: He gave up a lot for his family.
column9: Giving up a life or something valued for others or a cause: 為國犧牲, 犧牲自己, 犧牲睡眠. As a noun it is the cost itself: 很大的犧牲.

column3: Usually "relatively": 相对来说, 相对于 (compared with). As an adjective 相对的 "relative", opposite 绝对. It can also mean facing each other: 相对而坐. 相 first meant to observe, an eye looking at a tree, and was later borrowed to write "mutually".
column4: 相对来说，这里的房价比较便宜。
column5: 相對來說，這裡的房價比較便宜。
column6: Xiāngduì lái shuō, zhèlǐ de fángjià bǐjiào piányi.
column7: Relatively speaking, house prices here are cheaper.
column9: Usually "relatively": 相對來說, 相對於 (compared with). As an adjective 相對的 "relative", opposite 絕對. It can also mean facing each other: 相對而坐. 相 first meant to observe, an eye looking at a tree, and was later borrowed to write "mutually".

column3: A written "and" that mostly joins nouns (老师及学生); speech uses 和, and 以及 adds a last item. Its other sense, to reach, is in 及格, 及时 and 来得及 / 来不及 (in time / too late). It shows a person and a hand, "a hand grabbing a person".
column4: 老师及学生都可以参加。
column5: 老師及學生都可以參加。
column6: Lǎoshī jí xuésheng dōu kěyǐ cānjiā.
column7: Both teachers and students can take part.
column9: A written "and" that mostly joins nouns (老師及學生); speech uses 和, and 以及 adds a last item. Its other sense, to reach, is in 及格, 及時 and 來得及 / 來不及 (in time / too late). It shows a person and a hand, "a hand grabbing a person".

column3: A formal "and" or "with": 这与我无关, 与…有关, 与…不同, 与此同时 (meanwhile). Speech uses 和 or 跟.
column6: Zhè yǔ wǒ wúguān.
column7: This has nothing to do with me.
column9: A formal "and" or "with": 這與我無關, 與…有關, 與…不同, 與此同時 (meanwhile). Speech uses 和 or 跟.

column3: Opens a final sentence that sums up what came before, in speech and writing. The short form 总之 is more common, and 总的来说 is a softer version.
column4: 总而言之，这次考试很难。
column5: 總而言之，這次考試很難。
column6: Zǒng'éryánzhī, zhè cì kǎoshì hěn nán.
column7: In short, this exam was hard.
column9: Opens a final sentence that sums up what came before, in speech and writing. The short form 總之 is more common, and 總的來說 is a softer version.

column3: Formal "by means of" or "on the basis of" (以第一名的成绩). Mostly met inside words: 以前, 以后, 可以, 以免. 以为 is often used when the belief turned out wrong: 我以为你来了.
column4: 他以第一名的成绩毕业。
column5: 他以第一名的成績畢業。
column6: Tā yǐ dì yī míng de chéngjì bìyè.
column7: He graduated with the top grades.
column9: Formal "by means of" or "on the basis of" (以第一名的成績). Mostly met inside words: 以前, 以後, 可以, 以免. 以為 is often used when the belief turned out wrong: 我以為你來了.

column3: Seldom alone. The idea of passing through shows in 经过, 经历, 经验; 经常 is "often". It is also scripture: 佛经.
column6: Tā jīng cháng qù túshūguǎn.
column7: He often goes to the library.
column9: Seldom alone. The idea of passing through shows in 經過, 經歷, 經驗; 經常 is "often". It is also scripture: 佛經.

column3: A written, formal word, as in 著名 "famous" and 著作 "a written work".
column6: Tā zhù yǒu sān běn shū.
column7: He is the author of three books.
column9: A written, formal word, as in 著名 "famous" and 著作 "a written work".
